# Quick Study Guide: 7. Document Deletion & Collection Pruning (CRUD Delete)

> "deleteOne(filter) deletes the first document that matches a query filter. deleteMany(filter) deletes every document that matches a query filter. Passing an empty filter ({}) deletes all documents in the collection, without dropping the collection itself."

## 7.1 Document Deletion Execution Methods

> "deleteOne(filter) deletes the first document that matches a query filter. deleteMany(filter) deletes every document that matches a query filter. Passing an empty filter ({}) deletes all documents in the collection, without dropping the collection itself."

- **Single-Target Deletion: `deleteOne(filter)`.** `db.students.deleteOne({ name: "Kabir" })` finds the first document where `name` is `"Kabir"` and deletes it. Even if other documents also match, they stay safe.
- **Multi-Target Deletion: `deleteMany(filter)` & Empty Filter `{}`.** `db.students.deleteMany({ age: 17 })` deletes every student document where `age` is `17` (or `grade: 7`). If you pass empty curly braces `db.students.deleteMany({})`, MongoDB deletes every document in the collection, but keeps the empty `students` collection alive.

```javascript
// 1. Delete ONLY the first student named "Kabir"
db.students.deleteOne({ name: "Kabir" });

// 2. Delete EVERY student whose age is 17 (or grade is 7)
db.students.deleteMany({ age: 17 });
db.students.deleteMany({ grade: 7 });

// 3. Delete ALL documents in students, keeping the empty collection
db.students.deleteMany({});
```

| Command | What Gets Deleted | Does the `students` Collection Stay? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `db.students.deleteOne({ name: "Kabir" })` | First document named `"Kabir"` | Yes |
| `db.students.deleteMany({ age: 17 })` | All documents with `age: 17` | Yes |
| `db.students.deleteMany({})` | Every document in `students` | Yes (stays as an empty collection) |

---

## 7.2 Data Cleanup Architectural Tradeoffs

> "Passing an empty filter ({}) deletes all documents in the collection, without dropping the collection itself. db.collection.drop() permanently removes a collection and all of the documents it contains, along with any indexes defined on it. db.dropDatabase() permanently deletes the currently selected database, including all of its collections and documents."

- **Collection Purge: `db.<collection>.deleteMany({})`.** When you want to clear out all old documents from `students` but keep the `students` collection and its indexes ready for new records, use `db.students.deleteMany({})`.
- **Complete Collection Drop (`db.<collection>.drop()`) vs. Database Drop (`db.dropDatabase()`).** When you want to delete the `students` collection itself along with all its documents and indexes, use `db.students.drop()`. When you want to delete the entire active database (`schoolDB`) and every collection inside it, use `db.dropDatabase()`.

```javascript
// Option 1: Empty all documents, but keep the students collection & indexes
db.students.deleteMany({});

// Option 2: Delete the students collection, its documents, and its indexes
db.students.drop();

// Option 3: Delete the entire active database and all collections inside it
db.dropDatabase();
```

| Command | Documents Deleted? | Collection Kept? | Indexes Kept? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `db.students.deleteMany({})` | Yes (all in `students`) | **Yes** | **Yes** |
| `db.students.drop()` | Yes (all in `students`) | **No** | **No** |
| `db.dropDatabase()` | Yes (all in database) | **No** (all deleted) | **No** (all deleted) |

---

## Rapid Exam Trap Checklist

- `deleteOne(filter)` deletes only the very first matching document, even if many documents match.
- `deleteMany({})` with empty curly braces deletes all documents, but keeps the empty collection and its indexes.
- `db.students.drop()` deletes the entire `students` collection and its indexes, while `db.dropDatabase()` deletes the whole database.
